output.findings:
GitHub maintains a dedicated trending page for Python repositories, which updates daily and includes filters for 'This week'. Due to the dynamic nature of repository trends, specific rankings fluctuate based on recent star velocity and community activity.

While historical rankings often feature high-authority repositories like 'public-apis', 'free-programming-books', and 'system-design-primer' due to their massive long-term star counts, 'trending' status is determined by real-time engagement over the last 7 days. Users seeking the most current data should navigate directly to the GitHub trending Python page with the weekly filter applied.

output.final_answer: The most trending Python repositories on GitHub are determined by real-time star velocity and community engagement over the last 7 days. Because these rankings fluctuate daily, there is no single static repository that holds the title permanently. To see the most current list for the past week, you can visit the official GitHub Trending page for Python (https://github.com/trending/python) and select the 'This week' filter. Historically, repositories like 'public-apis', 'free-programming-books', and 'system-design-primer' frequently appear in top rankings due to their high long-term popularity.
